A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the measured posttensioned tendon losses were accurately predicted using the time-dependent analysis procedure specified by AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specification and the measured modulus of elasticity, shrinkage, and creep of the concrete girders.

the AASHTO LRFD method is adequate to predict tendon losses, but the method requires a better understanding of concrete shrinkage and creep properties, especially for concrete with high silica fume contents, and a more accurate method to determine the effective prestress force at the end of the posttensioning operation.
the AASHTO time dependent method predicts posttensioning loss in the precast, spliced, posttensioned girders with reasonable accuracy.

the measured posttensioned losses in the spliced, pre-cast girders were predicted reasonably well using the AASHTO LRFD time-dependent analysis method.

the time-dependent method for predicting tendon losses is a good method, but the accuracy of the method can be improved by conducting concrete tests on the concrete to obtain accurate values for the ultimate creep coefficient.
